verdict: First-year (2016) second-gen XC90 T6 (supercharged+turbo 2.0L Drive-E, 8-speed Aisin AWD). Middling reliability: average RepairPal rating 3.5/5, but first-year-of-generation electronics/software bugs, and complex twin-charged engine are expensive when they fail. 98k mi is low for the car, so condition depends heavily on service history. Poor choice for a strict <$1,000 budget but not the worst.
major_issues: Oil consumption complaints on T6 2.0L (NHTSA/CarComplaints, owner reports, often once past ~60-100k); 2 CarComplaints reports of total power loss (~62k mi, ~$20,000 engine repair, small sample); oil trap/PCV faults; Sensus infotainment/electronic glitches and early-VIN software issues; sunroof drain clogging (water leaks); air suspension (if equipped) failures ~$1,500-2,500 per corner; supercharger/turbo and coolant leaks (water pump/thermostat housing) $800-2,000 when they occur; transmission service/valve-body issues occasionally; 4-cyl timing chain failure not prominent in reports.
risk_reason: Only ~98k miles and RepairPal average is $851/yr, so a typical 6-month need is below $1,000, but luxury parts/labor mean any single failure (air suspension, coolant/water pump, sensors, supercharger, oil-consumption related) easily exceeds $1,000, and 2016 first-year models carry extra software/electronic risk. Unknown service history on an as-is auction car raises odds; catastrophic engine failure is rare but costs $10k+.
inspect_today: Cold start: listen for rattle/chain noise, supercharger whine; check oil level and condition (low/black = consumption or neglect), look for blue smoke on startup/revs; scan for stored codes and check all dash warnings (oil, coolant, City Safety, air suspension); check coolant reservoir level and for leaks around thermostat housing/water pump; pull oil cap/dipstick for milky residue; test AWD/8-speed shifts for harsh or delayed engagement; check for body/sunroof water stains in headliner and footwells and clear drains; test Sensus touchscreen, cameras, Bluetooth, power tailgate, HVAC; check if air suspension (if equipped) sits level and compresses; verify 3rd row seats, tire wear evenness, brake wear; run VIN for service records and recalls; confirm child-seat LATCH points work.
